classification.difficultyReason: Enumerate verbally described sets, compute their intersection and union, then transfer each result to a separate number-line representation.

content.prompt: In each part, list the elements of $A\cap B$ and $A\cup B$, then represent them on separate number lines.

answer.worked:
The only element common to both sets is 3, so $A\cap B=\{3\}$.

Collecting every element in either set without repetitions gives $A\cup B=\{0,1,2,3,6\}$.

On separate number lines, mark a closed dot at 3 for the intersection and closed dots at 0, 1, 2, 3 and 6 for the union.

children.prompt: $A=\{\text{odd numbers between 0 and 10}\},\ B=\{\text{whole numbers less than 6}\}$

answer.worked:
$A=\{1,3,5,7,9\}$ and $B=\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$.

The elements common to both sets give $A\cap B=\{1,3,5\}$.

Collecting every element in either set without repetitions gives $A\cup B=\{0,1,2,3,4,5,7,9\}$.

On separate number lines, mark closed dots at 1, 3 and 5 for the intersection and at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 9 for the union.
